children: China's problem isn't the cost of credit--it is the demand for it, say Ajay Rajadhyaksha and Amrut Nashikkar at Barclays Research. Corporate sentiment remains cautious despite a rebound in long-term lending. Corporate borrowing demand is being held back by weak domestic prospects, overcapacity and the continuing property-market downturn, and not because rates are too high, they say in a report. "That distinction matters because it means the PBOC has limited ability to help." Cheaper money doesn't solve a demand problem, they add. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)
